source_caption:
Timothée Chalamet and Matthew McConaughey recently reunited at the University of Texas for a CNN/Variety town hall, marking twelve years since they portrayed father and son in Interstellar. During the discussion, McConaughey surprised Chalamet by revealing that he has watched the film only once. He explained that revisiting his own performances feels emotionally demanding, adding that he generally avoids rewatching any of his projects.

Chalamet expressed genuine astonishment at the confession, noting his own deep admiration for the film. He shared that Interstellar remains his favorite project to date and that he has viewed it 22 times, including a private IMAX screening organized by Kylie Jenner for his birthday.

Reflecting on the experience, Chalamet spoke warmly about working with Christopher Nolan, whom he described as his favorite director. He credited The Dark Knight with inspiring his desire to pursue acting and cited Inception as a significant creative influence. Upon first reading the script for Interstellar, Chalamet recalled believing the film would have a profound cultural impact.

He also reflected on his youth during production, having been just 17 years old and newly graduated from high school. Observing the dedication and seriousness with which McConaughey and Nolan approached their craft left a lasting impression. Chalamet noted that the experience reshaped his perspective on acting and made returning to college particularly challenging.

source_details.title: Interstellar
source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
